newsitem.title: USA: Continental Air sees reaching labor pact.
newsitem.headline: Continental Air sees reaching labor pact.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc said it expects it will reach a labor accord with its pilots that offers increased compensation.

"Pilots deserve what's fair for the pilots. I don't know of any contract negotiations where the actual pay went down. So you would expect compensation to increase. The debate will be like -- what amount is fair?" said Continental chairman Gordon Bethune in a media teleconference Tuesday.

"I see no reason to have acrimony, disruption and heart burn. We have a company that's doing as well as it's doing. Each one of our pilots...is awfully proud of what's we've achieved. I don't think any group, especially not our pilots are going to want to disrupt that," Bethune said.
Continental's pilots receive about 35-40 percent less pay than the industry average, analysts said.
The pilots also will host a conference call later Tuesday to discuss the airlines' earnings and comment on labor issues.
Continental has already reached labor agreements with its mechanics, ramp agents and reservation agents.
"We have four or five (labor) agreements under out belt now, so we don't see any troubles," Continental's president Greg Brenneman said.
